text:
Connor Hellebuyck came to New Jersey after a holdout and won his first seven games as a Devil. On Wednesday a Montreal roster missing Chris Kreider and losing bodies by the week handed him his first loss, 3-2, and it was the Canadiens' rookie goalie who stole the night.

The first period had four goals in nine minutes. Luke Evangelista scored, Alex Newhook answered 40 seconds later, Timo Meier put New Jersey back in front with a backhand, and Nick Suzuki tipped in a power-play goal with 42 seconds left in the period. Lane Hutson assisted on two of those. Then nobody scored for more than 26 minutes, until Jake Evans finished a wrist shot in the third off a heads-up play by Oliver Kapanen, with Hutson on the assist again. That goal moved Montreal's win chance from 48% to 77%.

By our numbers the Devils had the better of it: 61% deserved to win (the share of replays of every shot each team wins), 67 shot attempts to 60, and a 1.04 expected-goals power play that came up empty in three tries, including two in the last 12 minutes. Jacob Fowler, the 69th pick in 2023 out of Boston College, made 28 saves, 1.7 goals better than the shots deserved, and added more to the win than anyone on the ice. His best stop came late, on Meier. Hellebuyck was ordinary, 25 saves on 28, right at expected.

Hutson finished with three assists in 26:42 and was the first star. Montreal also won 37 of 53 faceoffs. The Hockey News' Mike Fink called the Canadiens "the most skilled team the Devils have faced so far." For a Habs team dealing with injuries, and with Arber Xhekaj telling reporters some players are frustrated, a win on the road against the Devils' new goalie is the kind that steadies a week.

For New Jersey it is a loss to shrug at. They created enough. This time the goalie in the other net was better.
headline: Fowler hands Hellebuyck his first Devils loss
